text_in: Around 21 October 2024 (as reported), parents held a protest in front of the educational institution at Siriliguda village in Umerkote block (Nabarangpur, Odisha) demanding district-wise recruitment of teachers.

On 17 March 2023, members of AASU and several students staged demonstrations separately in Sivasagar city (Sivasagar, Assam) against the failure of state authorities to conduct free and fair class 10 HSLC examinations after multiple instances of leaked papers surfaced.

On 19 November 2024, activists of the Students Federation of India (SFI) staged a protest outside the district administrative complex in Gulbarga city (Kalaburagi, Karnataka), demanding re-examination to recruit Panchayat Development Officers (PDOs) and stringent action against those officers responsible for irregularities in conducting the examination. The protesters raised slogans against the KPSC and the INC-led state government.

On 6 February 2023, unemployed youths under the aegis of Rajasthan Berojgar Ekikrit Mahasangh (RBEM) gheraoed (surrounded) Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB) headquarters in Jaipur city (Jaipur, Rajasthan) demanding the release of the results of recruitment exams for the posts of physical training instructors (PTIs), laboratory assistants, librarians, firemen, and others. An RBEM delegation met the RSSB chairman and handed him a memorandum listing a series of demands

On 19 June 2024, medical professionals held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) to demand a judicial probe into irregularities in the conduct of the national level entrance examination for medical students.

On 26 March 2025, journalists staged a protest in Kachua village (Nagaon, Assam) against the arrest of a senior journalist who covered the protest against the financial irregularities and recruitment scam of Assam Cooperative Apex Bank the previous day (coded separately) and demanded his release, expressing their concerns over freedom of press.

On 16 November 2024, some diploma students along with a BRSV coordinator staged a protest at the State Board of Technical Education and Training in Hyderabad city (Hyderabad, Telangana), demanding the introduction of semester-wise supplementary exams in diploma programs and a resolution to the strict attendance policies. The protesters were detained by police.

On 16 May 2025, teachers under the banner of the Deserving Teachers' Association Rights Forum held demonstration march amidst an ongoing sit-in and vandalised guardrails set up by the police and RAF in Bidhannagar city (North 24 Parganas district, WB) against the school education department and the school service commission's decision to file review petitions before the Supreme Court, allegedly without consulting them in the 2016 recruitment exercise.

On 23 March 2024, AISF members held a sit-in protest and a day long hunger strike at Udhampur city (J&K) in support of the 21 day hunger strike called by prominent person in Leh to demand statehood for Ladakh, constitutional safeguards, recruitment, job reservation for the youth of Ladakh UT and creation of two separate constituencies for Leh and Kargil.

On 29 October 2024, students from Maharani's College belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) groups along with members of the AIDSO staged a protest outside the Crawford Hall at the University of Mysore in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the authorities for removing the 'zero fee payment' for SC and ST students. The protesters also demanded the authorities to extend the last date for the payment of the examination fees.
On 11 June 2024, members of INC, including the IYC state spokesperson, staged a protest in Ramnagar town (Nainital, Uttarakhand) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET 2024 results.

On 21 December 2023, dozens of students staged a protest in front of the Registrar's office of Maharaja Suheldev State University in Azamgarh city (UP), demanding action into claimed rigging in the distribution of question papers.

On 27 December 2023, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization), reached Rajgurunagar city (Pune, Maharashtra) and staged a protest march blaming the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' started from Bengaluru city on 10 December.

On 15 September 2023, a large number of rural women, minor boys and girls led by members of INC held a Jan Akrosh (people's anger) rally in Mhow city (Indore district, Madhya Pradesh) over issues of unemployment, inflation, and corruption in the state.

On 2 January 2024, several undergraduate students of Presidency University staged a protest in front of the campus in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding hall tickets for the upcoming semester exams. The protesters said that they were not being given hall tickers due to their low class attendance.

On 8 March 2023, JKSSB job aspirants held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the claimed grant of contract to Aptech limited for conduct of various exams as it was blacklisted. Police engaged in a baton charge and later detained several protestors.

On 5 March 2024, several youths held a protest at the district collectorate in Ajmer city (Rajasthan) demanding that the sub-inspector (SI) recruitment exam 2020 be conducted again by the Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC). They submitted a memorandum to the chief minister via the collector listing their demands.

On 13 January 2024, members of the Berozgar Sanjha Morcha (Unemployed United Front) staged a protest march, raising slogans, and burnt papers containing false promises (Larian Di Pand), along the Sangrur-Patiala Road towards the Chief Minister's residence in Sangrur city (Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of making false promises, and demanded the provision of government jobs.

On 9 July 2025, thousands of people, including farmers, banking employees, and members of various trade unions including the Punjab Roadways and Punbus Contract Workers' Union went on strike and staged protests in Amritsar city (Punjab) as a part of a nationwide call for strike made by a coalition of 10 major trade unions, including AITUC, INTUC, CITU, HMS, SEWA, LPF, UTUC, TUCC, AIUTUC, and SKM. The strike and protest was called over various demands including withdrawal of recruitment under Agniveer scheme, regularization of workers, hike in national minimum wage, withdrawal of the four new labor codes, loan waivers to farmers, Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, and a stop to the contractualization and privatization of the public sector departments.

On 4 April 2023, thousands of teachers from all Panchayats (village level local bodies) of Odisha under the aegis of NIOS DELED Teachers Association held a protest in the Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding several recruitments and perks for the private school teachers. The demands include a declaration of a pension policy for the private school teachers, giving priority to DEl.Ed teachers during the appointment in Government schools, the regularising job of NC- cleared Government teachers from May 22, 2019, and teachers of Catholic Mission Minority Board Schools.

On 9 December 2023, a large number of students staged a demonstration and vandalized and set fire to university property including chairs at the Sam Higginbottom University of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences (SHUATS) in Naini city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) against the new semester-end examination dates announced by the university. The students also engaged in a scuffle with the Vice-chancellor and the administration staff. No injuries were reported.

On 21 March 2025, TSF organized a road block protest as a part of the statewide protest and blocked the railway tracks in Jolaibari assembly constituency (South Tripura, Tripura) demanding the recognition of the Roman script for Kokborok language and the rescheduling of Kokborok board exams to implement it.

On 7 July 2024, SFI and DYFI staged a protest rally in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) with several demands including the resignation of Union Education Minister due to the recent NEET exam paper leak, scrapping of the National Testing Agency, reopening of shut-down government schools, provision of scholarships to financially weak students and stringent measures to curb drug abuse. Protesters also blamed the BJP government for the negative impact on education and employment sectors in Tripura.

On 10 February 2023, a group of people staged a protest in Rishikesh city (Dehradun district, Uttarakhand), against the government. They demanded an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into alleged paper leaks and government job recruitment scams in Uttarakhand.

On 4 July 2024, students affiliated to the AIDSO staged a protest at the Clock Tower in the Manasagangotri campus of the University of Mysore in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the BJP-led Union government over allegations of corruption and irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and the University Grants Commission-National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA). The protesters demanded an investigation and action against the accused.

On 20 June 2024, hundreds of students and members of NSUI, IYC, ABVP, SFI, Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS), AISA, and DSF staged a protest, raising slogans, and burned an effigy outside the residence of a Union Minister of Education (BJP) in Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi) condemning the education ministry for cancelling the University Grants Commission National Eligibility Test (UGC NET) examination. The protesters also demanded a ban on the National Testing Agency (NTA). Several protesters were detained.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Tiruppur city (Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 1 February 2024, Secondary Teachers' Graduate Test (STGT) job aspirants staged a protest at the Teacher's Recruitment Board Tripura (TRBT) office in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) demanding the prompt release of the pending 2022 exam results. They also demanded immediate collective appointments with no delay.

On 25 March 2023, members of Haryana Youth Congress staged a demonstration by burning tires in Gurgaon city (Gurgaon, Haryana) against the disqualification of an INC leader from the Lok Sabha, which they claimed was done to 'suppress opposition' as it raised demands for probe into the Adani Group and clarity on issues like unemployment. Four members were detained by the state police forces.
On 26 April 2024, students of Rama Devi Women's University held a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khorda, Odisha) demanding the postponement of the +3 second-year exam in the view heatwave.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Viluppuram city (Viluppuram, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 21 October 2023, members of the BJP held a protest at Ghatkopar (Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra), Bandra, Vile Parle, and Dahisar areas in Mumbai city (coded separately) against the previous state government led by INC, NCP, and Shiv Sena over introducing and implementing the contractual recruitment system in state government offices. The protestors demanded an apology from the opposition for misleading the people of Maharashtra.
On 27 December 2024, teaching job aspirants held a sit-in protest at Kolkata city (WB) to demand investigation into claimed irregularities. The sit-in ended on 12 February 2025.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC led by incumbent MLA (who was formerly the chief minister), as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in Raipur city (Chhattisgarh) against the claimed irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET)-UG examination.

On 22 June 2023, more than 500 unemployed graduates staged a protest march towards the Legislative Assembly in Puducherry city (Puducherry) demanding the Chief Minister to increase the Upper Division Clerk (UDC) seats. Protesters raised placards and slogans against the state government.

On 16 February 2024, 5 students went on a hunger strike and staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at the Lala Lajpat Rai University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences (LUVAS) in Hisar city (Haryana) demanding that theory and practical examinations be held within the campus area.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Narsinghpur district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 14 August 2024, members of the MDMK along with a former MP staged a protest near the Chidambara Nagar bus stop in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for not allocating sufficient funds to the state of Tamil Nadu in the 2024 Union Budget and for not cancelling the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate) (NEET) exam.

On 17 March 2025, a large number of officers of the Punjab National bank under the banner of AIBOC held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) over the newly implemented transfer policy and demanded an exemption for officers of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, equal and fair treatment to all trade unions and special recruitment under UDAAN program for Jammu Kashmir and Ladakh.

On 14 January 2024, members of the TDP including a former minister staged a protest in Anantapur city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for the price increase of commodities, the high rate of unemployment and other issues in the state.

On 25 September 2025, hundreds of job aspirants and members of All Karnataka State Students Association took out a protest march from Sri Nagar through College road to Jubilee Circle and staged a road block protest in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to fill vacancies. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 17 September 2023, members of IYC, including the State Secretary of IYC, staged an 'Unemployment Day' protest, raising slogans, and burned an effigy in Jalandhar city (Punjab) on the birthday of the Prime Minister of India (BJP) condemning the high rate of inflation and unemployment.

On 20 June 2024, students of Dhanamanjuri University (DMU) staged a protest rally towards the Chief Minister's residence in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the removal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in their campus and for the appointment of a new Vice Chancellor and Registrar to conduct their pending examinations amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters were intercepted at Ima Keithel, Kangla Western Gate and the Governor's residence but 30 of them were later allowed to meet the CM to present their demands.

On 9 April 2025, around 500 teachers and non-teaching staff held a protest as part of a statewide protest at Malda city (Maldah district, WB) against the TMC-led state government over claimed irregularities in the recruitment process and to demand reinstatement of teaching and non-teaching staff jobs invalidated by supreme court and publishing of their marksheets.

On 18 October 2023, students and guardians obstructed the entrance gate of Srimaa Ramachandi Government High School in Fatepur village in Kujang block (Jagatsinghapur, Odisha), to protest the untimely transfer of a teacher just three months before the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations.

On 21 June 2024, INC members, including a former MLA, led by its district president, staged a sit-in protest at Comrade Late Sarju Pandey Park in Ghazipur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams. The protest was part of a nationwide protest called by the All India Congress Committee (AICC). The protester scuffled (likely non-violent since no injuries were reported) with the police.

On 1 May 2023, Anganwadi workers, ASHA workers from across the state, and members of National Health Mission Employees' Union and B.Ed TET Pass Unemployed Teachers' Union gathered and staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's Office at BMC Chowk and Ladowali Road in Jalandhar City (Jalandhar-I, Punjab) against the unfulfillment of various promises made by the government, including regularization of jobs, and the exploitation of employees.

On 7 September 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a road roko (block) protest in Karur city (Karur, Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for the rise in prices of essential commodities and the increasing unemployment. Protesters demanded the Union government to take measures to control inflation, create job opportunities with social security and increase the allocation under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

On 31 July 2025, Staff Selection Commission (SSC) candidates and teachers staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in the Delhi - Connaught Place area (New Delhi, Delhi) against the suspected mismanagement of the SSC Selection Post Phase 13 recruitment exam. The police were suspected to have lathi-charged protesters. The protesters continued their protest and were later joined by an NSUI leader.

On 19 June 2023, JBT (Junior Basic Training) trainees, led by the Secretary of the JBT Trained Unemployed Union, staged a protest outside the Secretariat in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against irregularities in recruitment and the appointment of BEd candidates in the JBT cadre.
